intro: A zero of a polynomial p(x) is a value of x for which p(x) = 0. Graphically, zeroes are the x-coordinates where the graph of y = p(x) meets the x-axis. For a quadratic polynomial the zeroes are closely related to its coefficients.
keyPoints: A polynomial of degree n has at most n zeroes.
For ax² + bx + c with zeroes α and β: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.
A quadratic with sum of zeroes S and product P is k(x² − Sx + P), k ≠ 0.
To find zeroes, factorise and set each factor equal to 0.
